title: Characterizing Basement Membranes in Kidney Development Using Mass Spectrometry
author: Morais, Tian, et al.
materials: EDTA-free Roche complete protease inhibitor cocktail

steps.title: Reconstitute peptides and prepare LC‑MS/MS
steps.instruction: Reconstitute the dried peptides in 12 µL of 0.1 % formic acid in 3 % acetonitrile; calibrate the instrument as required and set up the Thermo Scientific Q Exactive HF hybrid quadrupole‑Orbitrap mass spectrometer coupled to a Dionex UltiMate 3000 RSLCnano system for peptide separation.

steps.title: Load sample onto CSH C18 column
steps.instruction: Transfer 1 µL of the peptide solution to a 5 µL autosampler loop, load onto a 75 mm × 250 µm, 1.7 µm CSH C18 analytical column (Waters) at a flow rate of 300 nL/min and run at 5 % mobile phase B for 5 min.

steps.title: Run LC gradient for peptide separation
steps.instruction: Apply the following gradient at the indicated flow rates: 5 % B to 7 % B while decreasing flow from 300 nL/min to 200 nL/min over 1 min; 7 % B to 18 % B over 64 min; 18 % B to 27 % B over 8 min; 27 % B to 60 % B over 1 min. Mobile phase A is 0.1 % formic acid in LC‑MS water, mobile phase B is 0.1 % formic acid in 80 % acetonitrile.

steps.title: Wash and re‑equilibrate column
steps.instruction: Wash the column at 60 % B for 3 min, then re‑equilibrate to 5 % B in 1 min; at 85 min increase the flow back to 300 nL/min and continue until the end of the 90‑min run.

steps.title: Acquire MS data with Q Exactive HF
steps.instruction: Operate the Q Exactive HF in HCD mode with data‑dependent acquisition of the top 12 most intense precursors (m/z 300–1750 Th, charge states 2‑4) and a dynamic exclusion of 15 s. Set MS1 resolution to 120 000, AGC target to 3 × 10⁶, maximum fill time 20 ms. Set MS2 resolution to 30 000, AGC target to 2.5 × 10⁵, maximum fill time 45 ms, isolation window 1.3 Th, collision energy 28 %. Run ECM fractions first, then cellular fractions, inserting blank runs between fractions and time‑points to avoid carry‑over.

steps.title: Import raw files into Proteome Discoverer
steps.instruction: Download the .raw spectra files to a local folder, open Thermo Scientific Proteome Discoverer, create a new study, add “Individual” factors for sample replicates and “Categorical” factors for experimental groups (e.g., Day 14, Day 18, Day 25), upload the .raw files in the Input Files tab, assign each file its categorical group and individual replicate in the Samples tab, and keep the Sample Type set to “sample”.

steps.title: Configure analysis workflows
steps.instruction: In the Analysis window select the Consensus step and open the workflow “CWF_Comprehensive_Enhanced Annotation_LFQ_and_Precursor_Quan” from the ConsensusWF folder; optionally set the Precursor Ions Quantifier scaling mode to none. Then select the Processing step and open the workflow “PWF_QE_Precursor_Quan_and_LFQ_SequestHT_Percolator” from the ProcessingWF_Qexactive folder. In the Protein FDR Validator node keep the default strict FDR = 0.01 and relaxed FDR = 0.05. Set the Protein Database to the appropriate SwissProt/TrEMBL version (v.2018_01) for Mus musculus or Homo sapiens. Use precursor mass tolerance 10 ppm, fragment mass tolerance 0.02 Da, and dynamic modifications of oxidation (+15.995 Da) on lysine (K), methionine (M) and proline (P).

steps.title: Run quantification and generate ratios
steps.instruction: In the Grouping and Quantification tab select the study variables (e.g., Day 18 vs Day 14, Day 25 vs Day 14, Day 25 vs Day 18) as denominators for protein ratio calculation, then execute the workflow to obtain label‑free quantification results.

steps.title: Export protein groups and identify ECM proteins
steps.instruction: Export the protein group results to an Excel file (.xls or .xlsx). Download species‑specific extracellular matrix and ECM‑associated protein lists from the Matrisome Project and basement membrane protein lists from bmBASE. Cross‑reference your protein list with these databases using gene symbols or UniProt IDs, retaining only proteins assigned to a unique protein group, identified by > 1 unique peptide, and classified as high or medium confidence (high: FDR 1 % and ≥ 70 % confidence).

steps.title: Create protein interactome in Cytoscape
steps.instruction: Export the filtered protein list as a short tabular text file, import it into Cytoscape, generate a protein‑protein interaction network with the STRING database using the stringApp plugin, customize the network as desired, and compute network topology parameters with the NetworkAnalyzer plugin.
